title: Burrata with Tomato and Basil
subtitle: Fresh burrata or buffalo mozzarella with heritage tomatoes and basil oil
excerpt: Burrata with tomato and basil is a summer antipasto that needs almost no cooking: a whole ball of burrata or buffalo mozzarella placed on a plate with the best tomatoes you can find, torn basil, and a generous pour of extra-virgin olive oil. The quality of every ingredient matters completely.
sourceNotes: Burrata originated in Puglia in the early twentieth century. The combination of fresh cheese with tomatoes and basil is one of the most iconic Italian antipasto preparations. Burrata, if unavailable, is substituted with mozzarella di bufala in many Italian restaurants outside Puglia.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Slice the tomatoes and season them up to 1 hour ahead. Add the cheese only at the last moment.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fresh Italian cheese from Puglia made from mozzarella formed into a pouch and filled with stracciatella (cream and pulled mozzarella). It has a firm outer shell but when cut releases a rich, creamy interior.

content.text: with tomato and basil follows the Italian principle that the best ingredients need nothing added. Cut open a whole ball of burrata and the creamy interior spills over ripe tomatoes dressed with flaked salt and good olive oil. Buffalo mozzarella works as a substitute when burrata is unavailable.

items.prepNote: balls of burrata or buffalo mozzarella, at room temperature
ripe mixed heritage or vine tomatoes

content.text: Remove the {{mozzarella-di-bufala}} from the fridge 30 minutes before serving. Cold cheese has no flavour or texture; room temperature is essential.

Core and slice {{tomato}} of tomatoes into thick slices or wedges depending on shape. Arrange on a serving plate. Season generously with {{salt-flakes}} of flaked salt and {{black-pepper}} of black pepper. Drizzle with {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil.

Tear the paper from the cheese (if packaged) and drain any excess liquid. Place the balls of burrata or mozzarella on top of the tomatoes. Scatter {{basil}} of torn basil leaves over everything and serve immediately with good bread.

items.cause: The cheese was served cold from the fridge, the tomatoes were unripe, or the olive oil was poor quality.
items.fix: All three components must be right: room-temperature cheese, ripe and well-seasoned tomatoes, and high-quality extra-virgin olive oil. There is nowhere for any of these to hide.

items.cause: The cheese was served cold, or it was low quality.
items.fix: Good burrata at room temperature should be soft enough to cut with the side of a fork. If it resists, it has either been refrigerated for too long or is a lower-quality product made for shelf life rather than immediate eating.

content.text: Burrata originated in Puglia in the 1950s as a way to use the cream and scraps left over from mozzarella making. The combination with tomatoes and basil follows the same tradition as caprese salad. The dish is at its best in summer, when good tomatoes and fresh burrata are both available. In Italian cooking, burrata with tomato is served as an antipasto rather than a salad. The cheese is the centrepiece; the tomatoes support it.
